title: If the bunker is completely flooded
question: Your ball comes to rest in a bunker that is completely filled with water and there is no dry ground to drop your ball inside the bunker. What should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from the water without penalty
Take free relief outside the bunker
Drop outside the bunker with a one-stroke penalty
Choose any spot on the course for free

explanation: If you cannot find a dry spot within the bunker, you are allowed to take relief outside the bunker, but you must take a one-stroke penalty.

juniorVersion.title: What if the whole bunker is under water?
juniorVersion.question: Your ball lands in a bunker, but the whole bunker is filled with water and there is nowhere dry to drop your ball inside. What can you do?

choices.text: Hit the ball out of the water with no penalty
Move your ball outside the bunker for free
Drop your ball outside the bunker, but add one shot to your score
Put your ball anywhere you want for free

juniorVersion.explanation: If there is no dry spot in the bunker, you can drop your ball just outside the bunker, but you must add one shot to your score.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A sandy area on the golf course, often next to the green or fairway.
Letting the ball go from your hand and letting it fall to the ground to play again.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show a picture of a flooded bunker and ask where you could drop the ball. Explain the reason for the extra shot.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think they can move the ball outside the bunker for free.
Some might believe they have to hit the ball from the water.
